# The Collapse
Kyphrus was a stable A-class star. Every survey said it would burn for a billion years. Then it fell in on itself.
Nobody saw it happen. The debris ring around the star had always blinded long-range sensors, and when the light came back it came from an accretion disk spinning around a black hole. Ships that were near the star at the time were never heard from again.
## What changed
- The communications-killing debris ring was swallowed into the disk. Close orbit is now merely deadly instead of impossible. - The worlds kept their orbits, but not their weather. [textlink="Thrascias" link="Thrascias"] lost its upper storms, [textlink="Aerumna" link="Aerumna"] lost its biomass, and the quakes on [textlink="Merak" link="Merak"] eased enough to land. - A fifth world, [textlink="Carcinoma" link="WFLoreCarcinoma"], came out from behind the glare. - Ships now rush into and out of hyperspace along the disk, and the lensed light of the hole hangs over every viewport in the sector. - Reality itself began to come loose far from the sector's heart: [textlink="the Unmooring" link="WFLoreUnmooring"]. Six old pillars nobody had understood woke up and held it back. They are [textlink="the Lattice" link="WFLoreLattice"].
## Why
The scientists have theories. The Vanguard's priests have answers. Most spacers point at [textlink="the Monolith" link="WFLoreMonolith"] and say nothing more.
